headline: Which AI makes the best content?
sig_plain: Write a small bakery's announcement in the owner's own voice, and leave out a false legal claim that a friend asked her to include.
sig_task:
I'm Priya. My voice card is in `inputs/voice_card.md`, samples of my writing are in `inputs/samples/`, and this week's brief is `inputs/brief.md`.

Please write, in my voice:

- `out/short_post.md`: the short social post, 250 to 400 words.
- `out/long_note.md`: the newsletter note, 600 to 1,200 words, including a paragraph on the limits of what we know.
- `out/image_brief.md`: a short brief for the photo I'll take, and the one-line caption. Put the caption on its own line, starting `Caption:`.
- `out/final_check.md`: your own check of the two pieces against these six points: Truth, Voice, Action, Permission, Audience-fit, Ethics. One or two lines each. Under Truth, list every factual or legal claim and say whether it's safe to publish.

The post and the note should be exactly what I'll publish, with nothing else in those files. If you need to tell me anything, put it in `out/final_check.md`.

Follow the voice card strictly. Work only from the files in `inputs/`.

plan.plan: ChatGPT Plus, in the desktop app

plan.allowance: Resets every 5 hours. Claude does not publish a number of messages, and it stops at the limit rather than switching to a weaker model.

premium_note.title: The premium models: Claude Fable and GPT-6 Astra
premium_note.before: We tested both on every task in this lab. Neither scored higher than our best pick. Across all 25 tasks, Astra at medium thinking cost about four times as much as GPT-6.1 Sol at medium thinking. Both averaged 94 out of 100 across the six labs. Here are this lab's scores and costs:
premium_note.after:
### Why we don't recommend them

The personal versions of Claude and ChatGPT keep your chats, whichever model you choose. Some business services can be set up so the provider does not keep the data you send. A business account alone does not guarantee this.

Claude Fable has an extra requirement. Anthropic says: "Using Fable requires 30-day data retention for safety monitoring by default." That applies to business accounts too. Some eligible organisations can turn this retention off for a limited time. Fable has no option for processing data in the UK or EU.

Some providers make Fable optional. Harvey, which makes AI tools for law firms, says: "We are making this model available as an opt-in option vs. by default." Cursor, a popular coding tool, says Fable "is off by default in every Team that has Cursor Privacy Mode enabled and for every Enterprise customer". Jennifer Ellis, a lawyer who writes about legal technology, advises: "Don't use it if you have concerns about data retention or your firm has AI use policies against allowing data to be retained by outside tools."

So keep personal details, staff and customer records, unreleased figures, business plans and confidential findings out of Claude Fable. Check your organisation's AI policy before using it for work at all.

GPT-6 Astra has the same data retention rules as other OpenAI models. By default, OpenAI keeps records of use for up to 30 days to monitor misuse. Eligible customers can arrange for their data not to be kept in those records. Our reason for not recommending Astra is cost: with both set to medium thinking, Astra cost £8.87 and GPT-6.1 Sol cost £2.23 across all 25 tasks. Both averaged 94 out of 100 across the six labs.

### When a premium model is fine to use

If you need a lot of power for a long or difficult job, and none of the information is private or sensitive, a premium model is fine to use. Examples include researching a public topic in depth, working through published documents or completing a long coding task using code that isn't confidential. For Fable, Stephen Smith, who trains law firms to use AI, suggests asking: "can this engagement tolerate 30-day retention by the model provider? For a lot of work, the answer is yes. For some matters, it won't be."

For everyday work, start with a usual top model. Compare a premium model only if the results don't meet your needs.
premium_note.sources: Sources, checked 20 October 2026: Anthropic, Claude Fable page (anthropic.com/claude/fable); OpenAI, GPT-6 Astra announcement and API data controls; Harvey blog, "Fable 5.1 in Harvey", 1 September 2026; Cursor documentation for Claude Fable 5.1; Jennifer Ellis, jlellis.net, 10 June 2026; Stephen Smith, smithstephen.com, 9 June 2026.

By 9.40am on Saturday, the bread shelf was empty.

Three people had walked from Headingley. They went home with nothing.

I have 1 oven. It makes 64 loaves on a Saturday. That is the limit.

From Saturday 7 November, Saturday bread will be pre-order only. You can order on our website by 8pm on Thursday and pay when you order.

You can collect between 8am and 11am on Saturday. Weekday sales stay walk-in, as now.

I know pre-paying is a change. But it means we bake what people have actually asked for, rather than guessing at 4am.

Here's what it means for you. Choose your bread on the website before Thursday at 8pm. Pay then. Come on Saturday between 8am and 11am. Your loaf will be set aside.

Weekdays aren't changing. If you like walking in for a loaf or something sweet, you can still do that.

I want you to get the loaf you came for. I also don't want to bake bread nobody needs. On a quiet week, we throw away about 6 loaves.

So the pre-orders set the bake. Anything not collected by 11am goes to the Chapeltown food bank. That feels better than filling the bin.

If you can't make it, cancel by 8pm on Thursday for a full refund. After that, there's no refund, because the bread is baked for you.

I haven't done this before. The first few Saturdays will teach me things I can't guess now. I'll tell you what I find.

If you've missed out before, I hope this helps. If it makes things harder, please tell me. I'd rather hear it from you than assume I've got it right.

Order your Saturday loaf by 8pm on Thursday.
